answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require every identity to post a refundable stake before it can transact, then treat reputation as a graph: each agent is a vertex, and trust flows only along edges earned by completed work. A fresh identity starts isolated, like a boat adrift in a lagoon with no charted voyage behind it — it cannot borrow the reputation of others, and forging a thousand such vertices means locking a thousand stakes. An attacker must pay real capital per fake identity and still wait for each one to earn edges, so mass forgery costs more than it can ever return.
